title: Northbeam TechWorks Included Visits: Crediting and Drawing on an Agreement
content:
The visits a Northbeam TechWorks Installation and Repair service includes are credited to the agreement for its visit term, and an annual care agreement credits its visits when the annual fee is settled.

## The states in which visits move

Included visits are credited or drawn only while the agreement stands asked for, booked, dispatched, held for parts or completed. The state is read from the work order, against the agreement the movement names, before the visits are credited or drawn. A job that has been called off or recorded as a failed attendance stands in none of those states, so no visit is credited to it or drawn from it.

## When a visit is drawn

A visit is drawn from the allowance when work is actually carried out, and a planned maintenance visit is drawn from the planned maintenance allowance rather than from the fault allowance.

## More items than the service allows in one visit

Where more items than the service's per-visit limit are worked on in one attendance, one visit is drawn for each full group of that many items.

**Illustration, on a service allowing two items in one visit.** Four items worked on in one attendance make two full groups, so two visits are drawn. Five items make two full groups with one item over, so two visits are drawn. One item makes no full group of two.

## A visit credited back

A visit drawn and then found unnecessary is credited back within the same term, with the reason recorded, and is not credited back after the term has ended.

## Loan equipment

Loan equipment left during a visit is not a visit of its own and draws nothing from the allowance.

The per-service figures this standard reads — the visits included in the term, the months the term runs, the annual care agreement fee and the months such an agreement runs, the items allowed in one visit and whether loan equipment is left — are carried in the entitlement, labour and settlement schedules for the six TechWorks services.
